bigPicture: AI agents are no longer prototypes — they're finding real vulnerabilities, deploying across 56,000-employee enterprises, and improving their own training, but the infrastructure to manage them (memory, sandboxing, orchestration) is barely keeping up.

dataPoints.context: Claude Opus 4.6 found real security bugs in production Firefox code with Mozilla
Toyota deploying AI agents at enterprise scale via LangChain — not a pilot, a rollout
Qwen 3.5 4B runs locally on consumer hardware — capable models escaping the cloud
Prediction within 10 years as AI collapses the team-size requirement for massive businesses

tldr: AI security research goes from theoretical to proven: Opus finds 22 Firefox vulns, OpenAI launches Codex Security, and research confirms models are better at finding vulnerabilities than exploiting them
Enterprise agentic adoption is real: Toyota's 56K-employee rollout and GPT-5.4 winning over finance teams with spreadsheets signal we've crossed the 'proof of concept' threshold
Karpathy's autoresearch validates AI self-improvement: distributed agent research (SETI@home model) is finding genuine training improvements, not just generating noise

The agent infrastructure gap is widening: CrewAI builds agents-managing-agents, Agent Safehouse tackles sandboxing, but context reuse and memory remain the critical bottleneck keeping agents in 'Groundhog Day'

The solopreneur signal keeps strengthening: on-device models, agentic frameworks like Paperclip, and the massive greenfield of legacy businesses still running on PDFs and phone calls point to a builder's market
